newsitem.title: USA: BankBoston studies national consumer units.
newsitem.headline: BankBoston studies national consumer units.

text.p: BankBoston said its national consumer lending businesses pose a "strategically complex challenge" and two senior executives will conduct a review with the goal of maximizing shareholder value.
News that BankBoston was looking at the businesses was contained in a memo Friday from chief executive Charles (Chad) Gifford detailing a new organizational structure.

The memo said vice chairman Edward O'Neal and William Ott, another top executive, will participate in the "expanded" effort to maximize value for the units. "Our national consumer specialty businesses present a strategically complex challenge," Gifford wrote.
He said while the businesses have been "significant contributors to the bottom line" at the same time that they are in "highly competitive markets where scale may become increasingly important."
He referred specifically to Ganis Credit Corp, which specializes in collateralized lending for recreational vehicles and boats, and Fidelity Acceptance Corp, a national consumer finance company.

In the BankBoston organizational changes, the "office of the chairman" is being replaced by a "policy council" of senior executives. Members will include Gifford, Chairman William Crozier, President and Chief Operating Officer Henrique de Campos Meirelles, Chief Financial Officer and Vice Chairman William Shea, and Paul Hogan, head of the corporate relationship bank and newly elevated to vice chairman.

Other members of the policy council include executives in charge of the major line businesses, and a group of executives heading corporate-wide committees on risk management, marketing and human resources.
Crozier, who headed the former BayBanks Inc, acquired in July, will focus on consumer banking and the overall regional business.
Crozier will make a formal recommendation on overall consumer strategy in early 1997, the Gifford memo said. He will also be active in visiting overseas offices.

BankBoston, which has extensive operations in Latin America, describes itself as New England's only global bank. It has 650 U.S. offices and more than 100 offices overseas, in Latin America, Europe and Asia.
BankBoston shares were up 1/2 to 57-1/4 in afternoon trading.
